If you tried to like RoR1 because of its great soundtrack, fun items, great atmosphere, and interesting universe, but couldn't truly love it because of its clunky gameplay, annoying navigation, and ridiculous difficulty, this game is unfortunately not going to be much more enjoyable for you.

There are wonderful graphical updates, some reworks to the soundtrack, some new characters, some new stages, and a few quality of life adjustments. Everything about the actual gameplay has remained pretty much unchanged.

It's saddening, because I really wanted to like the original, and was hoping the remake would be something I could finally get into. I was really excited to give it a try, and I tried, but I just don't feel like I'm having any fun. The worst part by far is I genuinely feel like nothing I do matters at all. I've tried prioritizing items, I lose. I've tried prioritizing time, I lose. I've tried kiting as much as possible, I lose. I've tried being aggressive, I lose. I've tried to fix the problem with the damage dealt/taken options, and it still feels completely unbalanced.

There is a lot to get used to, yeah i am a RoR2 player, did play a bit of 1 but did not play much after a single decent run. I am keen on giving it another chance with this though. 

The pixel work and animations are beautiful. It was really brought into modern pixel creativity and quality

The stuff to get used to: 
-You take a lot more damage all the time with almost no way to mitigate through movement and you do a lot less damage unless you get meta items or find coveted group killing items. 5s to kill a single enemy and you get overwhelmed FAST so you really have to pick battles and concentrate the enemies who can traverse for multi-hit/pierce skills. 
-Firing is a valuable commodity, your speed is halved when attack on most survivors so you can't run and gun, attributes heavily to doing less damage but i can see kiting would be a cheese strat 
-Unless i am completely missing things the item count is really barren especially in the first stage, likely to find just one outside the boss. 
-In RoR2 you could rush easier with portal particles since you could see across the map, you have to get ready to get unlucky finding the portal
-drones are significantly worse as they will float in melee range but looks like you can pay more to get them back.

would recommend ror2 first but if your here looking for more this game is great at doing just that.
if your also looking to play the first game this is the much better alternative.

I do agree with a lot of the points from the negative reviews, about how the game isn't changed enough from ROR1 and doesn't improve on ROR1 enough. Also, lots of mechanics from ROR2 could have been implemented here, as others point out. But, after spending 5 hours with the game, I want to jump right back in. So, I can recommend it. It's lots of fun, and joining random online co-op lobbies is great.

Also, the new Providence Trials are actually pretty fun I think.

Though, that is one negative point I have. The game could do a better job of explaining how co-op works. Do we share money for example? It doesn't explain that, as far as I know. Maybe I missed it.

Also, there REALLY should be a way to not pick up items in co-op. I've seen others bring this up as well. If you want your friend to have an item, there's no way to not pick it up. Adding the option, or making it default, to have to manually pick it up, would help a lot.

Honestly a VASTLY improved risk of rain 1 experience.  I would recommend this over the original, due to the graphics, animations, new items and survivors. The real meat of the game is the coop, with the ability to customize your runs with damage taken/dealt modifiers, and a slew of menu options. All that said for the price it is an incredibly buy and easily worth the time.  So if you bought 1 and 2 and liked them both definitely buy this one. Starting out is HARD for normal difficulty, so play around and see what works, MOST achievements are NOT difficulty restricted. This game is very accommodating and a fun time.

I thought I was basically insane for preferring ROR 1 over 2 but I think this re-release kind of vindicated the things I think ROR 1 does differently that I like so much. The gist of it is that 1 the length of the games are much shorter and the pace and difficulty of said games are harder and faster. You can knock out a game in ROR in under an hour basically and go "That was fun" and play another if you wish. Meanwhile the difficulty curve is much sharper, even on the harder difficulties in ROR 2 because the games are longer and the pace and even like speed at which your character moves reflects this, it takes much longer for the game to actually become difficult essentially where as Monsoon in ROR 1 is Immediately noticeable and consistently difficult. The upside of this too is that ROR 2 IMO has an issue where because the games are so much longer if your playing COOP and your on a losing streak that just compounds harder and over a longer time where you essentially will continue to die right away on a level and spend more and more time just watching other people play the game instead of you while alt-tabbing out or whatever where its much less of an issue in ROR 1 because of the faster pace shorter length of the games and consistent unrelenting difficulty. Hoppo has clearly understood this is an issue in general because Returns also has a "Drone Life" feature that is new that allows you to remain invested and involved in the game even after you die which is a stroke of genius on their part. 

TLDR: I thought maybe I was just looking at ROR 1 with rose tinted glasses but the remake proves that ROR 1 had its own qualities and features that make it stand out for me specifically and It really does kick ass like I thought.

Risk of Rain 1 was a better roguelike (imo!) than Risk of Rain 2, and a worse co-op game by virtue of being from the 2010's, before the world discovered things like "the internet". Risk of Rain Returns is, actually, not really a faithful remake as much as it is a proper sequel to Risk of Rain 1. in that vein it does pretty damn well! The art is gorgeous, the OST is fantastic, and the unlock system is *very* satisfying. 

I think there's a lot of conversations to be had about how the genre has progressed from the 2010's to now (and this is definitely more on the 2010's side of things) but ultimately, all i can say is this game *rocks*.

I think my sole complaint is that I think providence trials unlock a little *too* easily. I like that the alternate abilities are more accessible than they are in 2, but it feels weird to start getting them 3 hours into the game.  Otherwise 10/10! I hope it sees more support in the future.

It's a game that will not hesitate to beat your ass, but it's like in a kinky way so that you enjoy yourself.

Edit: I finally beat the game

the PERFECT remaster. it's a bottom-to-top rework, with flashy new art, animations, and sound in every detail. from an early ROR fan, I literally couldn't ask for more. everything special about the original is here, refined and improved, and with more added besides! 

THAT SAID, I think they cranked the difficulty a notch or twelve. at any difficulty, the enemy forces seem to scale much faster than we'd expect from those difficulties. Rainstorm's "Hard" feels more akin to "Insane", and it makes for an unfortunate "brick wall" effect where even good runs can be stymied by a sudden onslaught of elites that seem to arrive before they're invited. 
also, some characters (particularly new ones to this 2D paradigm) feel notably weak, especially Artificer. 
I suspect (and hope) that we'll see some patches to balance out the difficulty scaling and the underwhelming performance of some characters.
